name: APA Corporation
description: APA Corporation (parent of Apache) is an independent oil and gas producer with three producing areas: the US (mainly the Permian Basin), Egypt (where it is the largest acreage holder in the Western Desert and shares output with the state) and the UK North Sea, plus a development in offshore Suriname with TotalEnergies. It sells crude, NGLs and gas at market prices and resells some third-party volumes (purchased oil and gas sales). 2025 production was 169.5 MMboe and production revenue fell to $7,229M from $8,196M; the April 2024 acquisition of Callon Petroleum ($4.5 billion all-stock) added Permian acreage.

businessLines.name: United States
businessLines.how: Sells Permian Basin oil, NGLs and gas at market prices; Callon assets added in 2024; non-core New Mexico acreage was fully exited in 2025 (proceeds $571 million).

revenue.period: FY2025 oil, natural gas and NGL production revenue

businessLines.name: Egypt
businessLines.how: Sells oil and gas produced under production-sharing contracts in the Western Desert; part of production goes to the Egyptian government as cost recovery and profit share, and gas is sold largely to the state.

revenue.period: FY2025 oil, natural gas and NGL production revenue

businessLines.name: North Sea (UK)
businessLines.how: Sells crude and gas from offshore UK fields at market prices.

revenue.period: FY2025 oil, natural gas and NGL production revenue

businessLines.name: Suriname (development)
businessLines.how: No production yet; 50% working interest in Block 58 with TotalEnergies; first oil development (GranMorgu, FPSO with 220,000 b/d capacity, total investment estimated $10.5 billion) approved October 2024.

businessLines.name: Purchased oil and gas sales
businessLines.how: Buys third-party oil and gas and resells it; revenue is offset by purchase cost.

brands.name: Apache
brands.note: Operating brand of the E&P business; APA Corporation is the holding company.

brands.name: Callon Petroleum
brands.note: Acquired 2024-04-01 in an all-stock transaction valued at about $4.5 billion including debt.
